Data:Commit.bos.s.rites.theroots.json.label: What is Taken
Data:Commit.bos.s.rites.theroots.json.startdescription: The oldest living Hours are the gods-who-were-blood. The gods-from-Stone were older still, but they're buried in the earth, scattered in the sea, lost to the moon. This is why we're always careful where we make the sacrifice, because if we spilt enough blood on their graves, they'd return for their revenge. Bosk knows.
Data:Commit.bos.s.rites.theroots.json.desc: The oldest living Hours are the gods-who-were-blood. The gods-from-Stone were older still, but they're buried in the earth, scattered in the sea, lost to the moon. This is why we're always careful where we make the sacrifice, because if we spilt enough blood on their graves, they'd return for their revenge.

Data:Commit.bos.s.spices.savours.json.label: Served Cold
Data:Commit.bos.s.spices.savours.json.startdescription: Oak, earth, ice, ash, stars, blood. Drown to quenching. Serve. That's Bosk.
Data:Commit.bos.s.spices.savours.json.desc: Oak, earth, ice, ash, stars, blood. Drown to quenching. Serve.

Data:Commit.bos.s.tridesmahiera.json.label: The First among the Feasts
Data:Commit.bos.s.tridesmahiera.json.startdescription: The Moth consumed the Wheel; the Grail consumed the Tide; in the days of the Forge, the Stars fled from every facet of Flint. What feast was the first? Those who walk the Wood know that whichever was first, the Grail's was greatest.
Data:Commit.bos.s.tridesmahiera.json.desc: The Moth consumed the Wheel; the Grail consumed the Tide; in the days of the Forge, the Stars fled from every facet of Flint. What feast was the first? Those who walk the Wood know that whichever was first, the Grail's was greatest.

Data:Commit.bos.s.weaving.knotworking.js.label: What Endures
Data:Commit.bos.s.weaving.knotworking.js.startdescription: Cut a thread, and the tapestry must be healed. Bosk renews the weave.
Data:Commit.bos.s.weaving.knotworking.js.desc: Cut a thread, and the tapestry must be healed.

Data:Commit.hor.s.anbary.lapidary.json.label: Black Sapphire
Data:Commit.hor.s.anbary.lapidary.json.startdescription: The Bright Arts speak of a shining City Unbuilt. One day, we might build it in the Mansus, the great house of dreams… with a foundation-stone of black sapphire. This would be a great matter of Horomachistry.
Data:Commit.hor.s.anbary.lapidary.json.desc: The Bright Arts speak of a shining City Unbuilt. One day, we might build it in the Mansus, the great house of dreams… with a foundation-stone of black sapphire.

Data:Commit.hor.s.bells.brazieries.json.label: The Toll
Data:Commit.hor.s.bells.brazieries.json.startdescription: In the right mortal's hand, the right tool can become the weapon that begins a war. This is a high consequence of Horomachistry.
Data:Commit.hor.s.bells.brazieries.json.desc: In the right mortal's hand, the right tool can become the weapon that begins a war.

Data:Commit.hor.s.desires.dissolutions.j.label: Above
Data:Commit.hor.s.desires.dissolutions.j.startdescription: What begins in light may end in flesh. Without distinction and perception, pleasure cannot be distinguished from pain. These traditions are Horomachistry.
Data:Commit.hor.s.desires.dissolutions.j.desc: What begins in light may end in flesh. Without distinction and perception, pleasure cannot be distinguished from pain.

Data:Commit.hor.s.door.wall.json.label: What Should Not Be
Data:Commit.hor.s.door.wall.json.startdescription: There is a prophecy, of a shining City that mortals might build. There is a paradox, that a City Unbuilt can always be greater than one that exists. The Bright Arts teach this resolution: that the Hours will always forbid the raising of that City, so that it will remain a great hope and a great travelling.
Data:Commit.hor.s.door.wall.json.desc: There is a prophecy, of a shining City that mortals might build. There is a paradox, that a City Unbuilt can always be greater than one that exists. The Bright Arts teach this resolution: that the Hours will always forbid the raising of that City, so that it will remain a great hope and a great travelling.

Data:Commit.hor.s.drums.dances.json.label: The Heart
Data:Commit.hor.s.drums.dances.json.startdescription: The Thunderskin, the eternal drum that beats to preserve the skin of the world, is a god-from-flesh, which is to say he was once mortal. But the Horned-Axe, last of the gods-from-stone, required his death, and so the Grail gave him up, though he loved her. Love is always subject to the will of the Hours, as all horomachists know.
Data:Commit.hor.s.drums.dances.json.desc: The Thunderskin, the eternal drum that beats to preserve the skin of the world, is a god-from-flesh, which is to say he was once mortal. But the Horned-Axe, last of the gods-from-stone, required his death, and so the Grail gave him up, though he loved her. Love is always subject to the will of the Hours, as all horomachists know.

Data:Commit.hor.s.edictsinviolable.json.label: Fire
Data:Commit.hor.s.edictsinviolable.json.startdescription: The Mare-in-the-Tree is not the youngest Hour; but she is the youngest Hour of Calyptra, for she has been born many times in many places. The Red Flower on the Watchman's Tree is the fire fuelled by truth, and without it the Tree would fall, as all horomachists know.
Data:Commit.hor.s.edictsinviolable.json.desc: The Mare-in-the-Tree is not the youngest Hour; but she is the youngest Hour of Calyptra, for she has been born many times in many places. The Red Flower on the Watchman's Tree is the fire fuelled by truth, and without it the Tree would fall.

Data:Commit.hor.s.edictsmartial.json.label: Conflict Creates Gods
Data:Commit.hor.s.edictsmartial.json.startdescription: All the Hours are defined by their opposition to other Hours... just as we are defined by the battles we choose. This is a matter of the Horomachistry Wisdom.
Data:Commit.hor.s.edictsmartial.json.desc: All the Hours are defined by their opposition to other Hours... just as we are defined by the battles we choose. This is a matter of the Horomachistry Wisdom.

Data:Commit.hor.s.inks.containment.json.label: When It Is Permitted
Data:Commit.hor.s.inks.containment.json.startdescription: Certain knowledge is forbidden to mortals… unless it's wisely contained. This law is named Calyptra; the enforcement of this law is named Calyptra also; the three Hours who enforce it share that name. They permit that knowledge to persist only in certain sanctioned places, and the most dangerous secrets must only be recorded in the inks called encaustum terminale. Horomachistry teaches us Calyptra's importance.
Data:Commit.hor.s.inks.containment.json.desc: Certain knowledge is forbidden to mortals… unless it's wisely contained. This law is named Calyptra; the enforcement of this law is named Calyptra also; the three Hours who enforce it share that name. They permit that knowledge to persist only in certain sanctioned places, and the most dangerous secrets must only be recorded in the inks called encaustum.

Data:Commit.hor.s.inks.power.json.label: The Weapon
Data:Commit.hor.s.inks.power.json.startdescription: The greatest and most secret truths can only be recorded by the Librarians of the Watchman's Tree - even then, only beneath the shelter of the Tree's branches, and only in the sanctioned inks called encaustum. There are still certain languages in which these truths might be spoken aloud, but the Hours no longer permit that power in the mouths of mortals, as the wisdom of Horomachistry teaches us.
Data:Commit.hor.s.inks.power.json.desc: The greatest and most secret truths can only be recorded by the Librarians of the Watchman's Tree - even then, only beneath the shelter of the Tree's branches, and only in the sanctioned inks called encaustum. There are still certain languages in which these truths might be spoken aloud, but the Hours no longer permit that power in the mouths of mortals.

Data:Commit.hor.s.mandaic.json.label: The Jeweller's Tale
Data:Commit.hor.s.mandaic.json.startdescription: There is a story known to jewellers: of a guild-master who made a wager with a keeper of butterflies. The master-jeweller claimed his jewelled egg would hatch something greater than any of the butterfly-keeper's chrysalids. Of course, after a month, the butterfly-keeper's gardens were bright with wings and the egg had hatched nothing at all. The jeweller, unable to pay his debts, fled into the desert with his egg. Horomachistry teaches us: know your limits.
Data:Commit.hor.s.mandaic.json.desc: A master jeweller who made a wager with a keeper of butterflies. The master-jeweller claimed his jewelled egg would hatch something greater than any of the butterfly-keeper's chrysalids. Of course, after a month, the butterfly-keeper's gardens were bright with wings and the egg had hatched nothing at all. The jeweller, unable to pay his debts, fled into the desert with his egg. Perhaps we should be careful of our limits.

Data:Commit.hor.s.ouranoscopy.json.label: Peace
Data:Commit.hor.s.ouranoscopy.json.startdescription: If night is peace, then dawn is battle, when the Sun drives the stars from the sky. A day might come when the Sun's victory is not assured. The battles of heaven are a matter of Horomachistry.
Data:Commit.hor.s.ouranoscopy.json.desc: If night is peace, then dawn is battle, when the Sun drives the stars from the sky. A day might come when the Sun's victory is not assured.

Data:Commit.hor.s.sabazine.json.label: The Sailor's Tale
Data:Commit.hor.s.sabazine.json.startdescription: There's a story told by sailors, about a city of ivory and iron across the sea. Those who come there never die, but those who leave again have never lived. Only in another History, they say; but if you rig your sails right, you might just catch the wind that takes you there in this one.
Data:Commit.hor.s.sabazine.json.desc: There's a story told on the sea, about a city of ivory and iron across the sea. Those who come there never die, but those who leave again have never lived. Only in another History, they say; but if you rig your sails right, you might just catch the wind that takes you there in this one.

Data:Commit.hor.s.sacralimiae.json.label: Of Limits
Data:Commit.hor.s.sacralimiae.json.startdescription: The Hours are not all-powerful. There is a place beyond their reach, where mortals and immortals might build a shining City of iron and ivory. Horomachists understand the Hours' limits.
Data:Commit.hor.s.sacralimiae.json.desc: The Hours are not all-powerful. There is a place beyond their reach, where mortals and immortals might build a shining City of iron and ivory.

Data:Commit.hor.s.sacrasolisinvicti.json.label: A Light Above
Data:Commit.hor.s.sacrasolisinvicti.json.startdescription: The New King's light shines brightly. The Sanctioned Version of the Book of Suns tells us that he may herald the unification of the gods-who-were-Light, into a new Sun-in-Splendour.  We should seek answers in Horomachistry.
Data:Commit.hor.s.sacrasolisinvicti.json.desc: The New King's light shines brightly. The Sanctioned Version of the Book of Suns tells us that he may herald the unification of the gods-who-were-Light, into a new Sun-in-Splendour.

Data:Commit.hor.s.skystories.json.label: The Tryst
Data:Commit.hor.s.skystories.json.startdescription:
The Pilgrim's intrigue and the Grail's scheme
The Sun in shadow and the Forge unseen
The Swan King and the Elagabaline.

This is Horomachistry.
Data:Commit.hor.s.skystories.json.desc:
The Pilgrim's intrigue and the Grail's scheme
The Sun in shadow and the Forge unseen
The Swan King and the Elagabaline.

Data:Commit.hor.s.thegreatsignsandthegre.label: The First Enemy
Data:Commit.hor.s.thegreatsignsandthegre.startdescription: Vak is a Great Scar; the first enemy of Calyptra. When the black flower blossoms on the Watchman's tree, she retreats, and Calyptra protects perilous knowledge behind secrecy's veil. The nature of their enmity is a Horomachistry matter.
Data:Commit.hor.s.thegreatsignsandthegre.desc: Vak is a Great Scar; the first enemy of Calyptra. When the black flower blossoms on the Watchman's tree, she retreats, and Calyptra protects perilous knowledge behind secrecy's veil.

Data:Commit.hus.s.disciplines.thescar.js.label: The Crime
Data:Commit.hus.s.disciplines.thescar.js.startdescription: The Mansus is the fortress in dream raised by the gods-who-were-stone. Nowhere is the inevitable scar beneath it. Monstrous, the gods-from-Nowhere; but cruel, the gods-who-were-stone.
Data:Commit.hus.s.disciplines.thescar.js.desc: The Mansus is the fortress in dream raised by the gods-who-were-stone. Nowhere is the inevitable scar beneath it. it. Monstrous, the gods-from-Nowhere; but cruel, the gods-who-were-stone.

Data:Commit.hus.s.ericapaean.json.label: The King in the Mirror
Data:Commit.hus.s.ericapaean.json.startdescription:
There is a story told by students of silence: that a great and golden King held the only key to his deepest prison cell. One day he gave the key to his minister, and offered him a choice: to submit to execution, or to visit the cell and tell him what he found there. The minister made the wiser choice, and returned to show the King what he had found in the cell: a mirror.

'Then I release you,' the King declared. The minister left the palace that same day. His reflection, of course, said nothing at all.
Data:Commit.hus.s.ericapaean.json.desc:
A great and golden King held the only key to his deepest prison cell. One day he gave the key to his minister, and offered him a choice: to submit to execution, or to visit the cell and tell him what he found there. The minister made the wiser choice, and returned to show the King what he had found in the cell: a mirror.

'Then I release you,' the King declared. The minister left the palace that same day. His reflection, of course, said nothing at all.

Data:Commit.hus.s.fucine.json.label: The Queen's Wound
Data:Commit.hus.s.fucine.json.startdescription: There is a story known to painters: of a Queen who could love no other, neither woman nor man, but only her own image. She sought nine colours to grace the image, and the last was the turquoise of her eyes, a gift from the Shadowless King. Her court poet hymned his Queen and her image, and in his poem she heard the truth: that the image was greater. So she fled into the Wood, and the image ruled her domain with the poet as its consort, but it always remembered her kindly.
Data:Commit.hus.s.fucine.json.desc: A Queen could love no other, only her own image. She sought nine colours to grace the image, and the last was the turquoise of her eyes, a gift from the Shadowless King. Her court poet hymned his Queen and her image, and in his poem she heard the truth: that the image was greater. So she fled into the Wood, and the image ruled her domain with the poet as its consort, but it always remembered her kindly.

Data:Commit.hus.s.glassblowing.vesselcra.label: Glass, the Keeper
Data:Commit.hus.s.glassblowing.vesselcra.startdescription: The highest purpose of a glass vessel: to separate what is without from what is within. Perhaps, Hushery suggests, this was the first purpose of the first Hour, and only in that first moment could there be perfect understanding.
Data:Commit.hus.s.glassblowing.vesselcra.desc: The fundamental purpose of a glass vessel: to separate what is without from what is within. Perhaps this was the first purpose of the first Hour, and only in that first moment could there be perfect understanding.

Data:Commit.hus.s.inks.power.json.label: The Wound
Data:Commit.hus.s.inks.power.json.startdescription: The greatest and most secret truths can only be recorded by the Librarians of the Watchman's Tree - even then, only beneath the shelter of the Tree's branches, and only in the sanctioned inks called encaustum terminale. There are still certain languages in which these secrets can be spoken aloud, but that has never been safe. These secrets are the world's blood, and to speak them aloud is to shed that blood. We who are silent have always known this.
Data:Commit.hus.s.inks.power.json.desc: The greatest and most secret truths can only be recorded by the Librarians of the Watchman's Tree - even then, only beneath the shelter of the Tree's branches, and only in the sanctioned inks called encaustum terminale. There are still certain languages in which these secrets can be spoken aloud, but that has never been safe. These secrets are the world's blood, and to speak them aloud is to shed that blood.

Data:Commit.hus.s.inks.revelation.json.label: Truths that Were
Data:Commit.hus.s.inks.revelation.json.startdescription: The inks called encaustum terminale are permitted only to the Librarians of the Watchman's Tree. Those inks can be used to reveal truths - even truths that are no longer so, not since the dawn times when the sun hung red and low and we felt its warmth like autumn. If that first and gentlest sun returned, the truths might return with it. Hushery remembers.
Data:Commit.hus.s.inks.revelation.json.desc: The inks called encaustum terminale are permitted only to the Librarians of the Watchman's Tree. Those inks can be used to reveal truths - even truths that are no longer so, not since the dawn times when the sun hung red and low and we felt its warmth like autumn. If that first and gentlest sun returned, the truths might return with it.

Data:Commit.hus.s.maggephenemysteries.js.label: Revenge
Data:Commit.hus.s.maggephenemysteries.js.startdescription: The gods-who-are, which we call the Hours, warred against the gods-from-stone and cast them down. What remains of the gods-from-stone we call plague, scourge, catastrophe. If the Hours were cast down in their turn, would the gods-from-stone be satisfied? Would revenge bring peace? The Night Arts hint that it might be so.
Data:Commit.hus.s.maggephenemysteries.js.desc: The gods-who-are, which we call the Hours, warred against the gods-from-stone and cast them down. What remains of the gods-from-stone we call plague, scourge, catastrophe. If the Hours were cast down in their turn, would the gods-from-stone be satisfied? Would revenge bring peace? The Night Arts hint that it might be so.

Data:Commit.hus.s.ouranoscopy.json.label: Wisdom
Data:Commit.hus.s.ouranoscopy.json.startdescription: If the stars are wisdom, then dawn is ignorance. A day might come when there is no dawn. Ouranoscopy should be numbered among the Night Arts.
Data:Commit.hus.s.ouranoscopy.json.desc: If the stars are wisdom, then dawn is ignorance. A day might come when there is no dawn.

Data:Commit.hus.s.quenchings.quellings.j.label: Safety in Silence
Data:Commit.hus.s.quenchings.quellings.j.startdescription: Unwise words are dangerous. Mourn them, remember them, speak them not. This is Hushery.
Data:Commit.hus.s.quenchings.quellings.j.desc: Unwise words are dangerous. Mourn them, remember them, speak them not.

Data:Commit.hus.s.sacralimiae.json.label: Of Endings
Data:Commit.hus.s.sacralimiae.json.startdescription: The Hours are not eternal. The Sun-in-Splendour was riven and cast down. If we mortals so desire, we might prevent his return. Understand Hushery, and you understand endings.
Data:Commit.hus.s.sacralimiae.json.desc: The Hours are not eternal. The Sun-in-Splendour was riven and cast down. If we mortals so desire, we might prevent his return.

Data:Commit.hus.s.serpents.venoms.json.label: The Last Sun
Data:Commit.hus.s.serpents.venoms.json.startdescription: In the dawn times the sun was lower, so we gave it our blood. From our blood it knew us, and so it was kinder. Its serpents brought us its poisons to drink, and so we died. But we only died a little, and so we dreamed, and returned the next day to give it our blood again. Those times of peace persist in the lessons of Hushery.
Data:Commit.hus.s.serpents.venoms.json.desc: In the dawn times the sun was lower, so we gave it our blood. From our blood it knew us, and so it was kinder. Its serpents brought us its poisons to drink, and so we died. But we only died a little, and so we dreamed, and returned the next day to give it our blood again.

Data:Commit.hus.s.sharps.json.label: A Wound in Dreams
Data:Commit.hus.s.sharps.json.startdescription: Before speech, we could not dream, which is to say that before speech tore open the Peacock Gate to dreams, the Mansus was unwounded and at peace. It's not obligatory for Long to pass that gate, but they generally choose to. Perhaps that's why the Hours charge their Names to hunt down Long - even the Long who claim to serve them. Hushery recognises this truth.
Data:Commit.hus.s.sharps.json.desc: Before speech, we could not dream, which is to say that before speech tore open the Peacock Gate to dreams, the Mansus was unwounded and at peace. It's not obligatory for Long to pass that gate, but they generally choose to. Perhaps that's why the Hours charge their Names to hunt down Long - even the Long who claim to serve them.

Data:Commit.hus.s.sights.sensations.json.label: The End
Data:Commit.hus.s.sights.sensations.json.startdescription: The artist knows: their every work could be improved. The artist understands: perfect work can never be completed. Perfection exists only as absence: Hushery understands this.
Data:Commit.hus.s.sights.sensations.json.desc: The artist knows: their every work could be improved. The artist understands: perfect work can never be completed.

Data:Commit.hus.s.snowstories.json.label: Much is Lost
Data:Commit.hus.s.snowstories.json.startdescription:
Still all the winds, still every beating tongue
Now still the mirrored moon, the sea's cauldron
When nothing's left then nothing is undone.

Hushery.
Data:Commit.hus.s.snowstories.json.desc:
Still all the winds, still every beating tongue
Now still the mirrored moon, the sea's cauldron
When nothing's left then nothing is undone.

Data:Commit.hus.s.surgeries.exsanguinati.label: The White
Data:Commit.hus.s.surgeries.exsanguinati.startdescription: The Watchman's Tree has flowers three: Black, Red, and White. Red is the life that flows in the body's courses, and white is the writing at the body's core. Hushery teaches what ends.
Data:Commit.hus.s.surgeries.exsanguinati.desc: The Watchman's Tree has flowers three: Black, Red, and White. Red is the life that flows in the body's courses, and white is the writing at the body's core.

Data:Commit.hus.s.thegreatsignsandthegre.label: The First Error
Data:Commit.hus.s.thegreatsignsandthegre.startdescription: Vak is a Great Scar; Calyptra's first mistake. If she could only be healed of her pain, Calyptra might reign inviolate, and the perilous knowledge it protects might be truly safe. The nature of her healing is a Hushery matter.
Data:Commit.hus.s.thegreatsignsandthegre.desc: Vak is a Great Scar; Calyptra's first mistake. If she could be healed of her pain, Calyptra might reign inviolate, and the perilous knowledge it protects might be truly safe.

Data:Commit.ill.s.applebrighteuphonies.j.label: What May Be True
Data:Commit.ill.s.applebrighteuphonies.j.startdescription: Calyptra is the law that requires secret knowledge to be forgotten - except in the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. The number of the Hours of the Calyptra is three, and we do not trust the third Hour, though we heed her. This paradox is a matter of Illumination.
Data:Commit.ill.s.applebrighteuphonies.j.desc: Calyptra is the law that requires secret knowledge to be forgotten - except in the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. The number of the Hours of the Calyptra is three, and we do not trust the third Hour, though we heed her.

Data:Commit.ill.s.auroralcontemplations..label: The First Sunrise
Data:Commit.ill.s.auroralcontemplations..startdescription: Yesterday's light determines the colours of tomorrow... and through Illumination, we learn that we all began in light.
Data:Commit.ill.s.auroralcontemplations..desc: Yesterday's light determines the colours of tomorrow...  and we all began in light.

Data:Commit.ill.s.cracktrack.json.label: A Tongue of Sky
Data:Commit.ill.s.cracktrack.json.startdescription: Cracktrack was a gift from the light above the world. When Glory touched the first life-motes with this language, they entered the waking world. They were Illuminated.
Data:Commit.ill.s.cracktrack.json.desc: Cracktrack was a gift from the light above the world. When Glory touched the first life-motes with this language, they entered the waking world.

Data:Commit.ill.s.disciplines.thehammer..label: Steel and Glass
Data:Commit.ill.s.disciplines.thehammer..startdescription: A certain parable of the Bright Arts tells of a priest who raised an altar of steel and glass to an old god; but then found a new god within the altar.
Data:Commit.ill.s.disciplines.thehammer..desc: A certain parable of the Bright Arts tells of a priest who raised an altar of steel and glass to an old god; but then found a new god within the altar.
